answers.rationale: I'd definitely use this feature if I could see the diffs first. Being able to review changes before accepting them is exactly what I need to trust an agent with my code. That transparency is crucial for me.

Knowing I can roll back to a checkpoint if something goes wrong would give me real peace of mind. It's the safety net that lets me actually let the agent do more complex work without constantly second-guessing it.

My biggest fear is that the agent makes subtle bugs or logic errors that I don't catch in review. It's easy to miss mistakes, especially in complex logic. I'd rather have a tool that's conservative than one that breaks my codebase in hard-to-spot ways.

answers.value: Refactoring variable names and formatting code in a well-tested module with good test coverage
answers.rationale: I'd start with low-risk mechanical changes—things like renaming variables or cleaning up formatting in code that's already well-tested. If the agent messes up, the tests will catch it. That's a safe way to build trust before delegating more complex logic changes.
